mode.name: FAQ
mode.description: Answers one concrete question the audience is already asking.
mode.structure: The question (as the audience would ask it) -> honest answer -> why it matters -> CTA.
mode.avoid: Do not invent a fake FAQ; use a real audience question grounded in Product Brain.

hook.instruction: Open on a sharp before/after or this-vs-that contrast.
hook.exampleForm: "Two hours of scrubbing vs fifteen minutes done right."
hook.forbidGeneric: Do not open with "There are many ways to do this."

concept.title: The Only Thing fenrik Studio Needs From You
concept.core_idea: Most people stall before they ever submit anything because they assume a content service requires a creative brief, platform strategy, tone guidelines, and a kickoff call. This video answers the one question silently blocking conversion: 'What do I actually have to give you?' The answer is a URL. Nothing else. The first package is free. The barrier people imagined does not exist.
concept.product_role: fenrik Studio is the proof that collapses the imagined barrier. It is not described as a tool or a platform — it is described as a service that already has what it needs the moment a website URL exists. The free first package is the CTA mechanism: it removes cost as a secondary barrier once the input barrier is already gone.
concept.why_it_works: The FAQ mode is used honestly — this is a real question blocking real conversions. The contrast hook (imagined input vs actual input) is visually and cognitively immediate. The reporter voice keeps it credible: no hype, just a plain answer to a plain question. The concept is distinct from all recent fingerprints: no team workspace, no analytics dashboard, no late-night founder scene, no agency meeting room. The visual world is a clean split-screen or side-by-side graphic treatment — entirely typographic and interface-native — which has not appeared in the recent production run.
concept.narrative_arc: QUESTION (contrast hook): Open on a sharp before-after contrast — one side is the imagined input (a brief, a brand doc, a call, a strategy deck), the other side is the actual input (a website URL, typed in ten seconds). The contrast is stated plainly, no drama. ANSWER: The video explains directly that fenrik Studio reads the website, builds the content, and delivers a complete package — video, captions, hashtags, platform-ready for every channel — from that single input. No direction required from the client. WHY IT MATTERS: Most people never start because they are waiting until they have time to write the brief. That moment never arrives. The brief was always the invisible barrier. Here it does not exist. CTA: Submit the URL. The first package is free. There is nothing left to prepare.
concept.emotional_tone: Matter-of-fact and quietly reassuring — no pressure, no urgency theater. The tone is a reporter stating a fact the audience did not know but immediately believes. Relief, not excitement.
concept.audience_insight: The audience has mentally queued fenrik Studio under 'things I need to set up properly before I start' — alongside writing a brand brief, scheduling a discovery call, and deciding on a content strategy. That queue never clears. The video removes the queue entirely by showing that the setup they imagined was never required.

visual_direction.palette: White or very light grey background. The 'imagined input' list in muted mid-grey. The URL line and fenrik Studio branding in a single strong accent color — deep navy or near-black. One accent highlight color (e.g. a clean amber or teal) used only on the word 'free' in the CTA card.
visual_direction.lighting: Flat, even digital light — no shadows, no warmth, no atmosphere. This is a screen-native visual, not a location shoot.
visual_direction.environment: No physical environment. The entire visual world is a sequence of typographic cards or a split-screen graphic — designed to feel like a product interface or a clean explainer slide, not a filmed location.
visual_direction.camera_style: No camera. Motion is handled through card transitions — a clean slide or fade from the 'imagined input' card to the 'actual input' card. Text appears with minimal, purposeful timing. No zoom, no parallax, no cinematic movement.
visual_direction.art_direction: Clean split-screen or sequential card treatment. Left card (or first card): a stacked list of imagined inputs — 'Brand brief. Tone guidelines. Platform strategy. Kickoff call.' — rendered in a slightly faded, greyed-out typeface as if crossed off or irrelevant. Right card (or second card): a single line — 'Your website URL.' — in clean, confident type at full opacity. No illustration, no stock photography. Pure typographic contrast.

product_role: fenrik Studio is the proof that collapses the imagined barrier. It is not described as a tool or a platform — it is described as a service that already has what it needs the moment a website URL exists. The free first package is the CTA mechanism: it removes cost as a secondary barrier once the input barrier is already gone.
narrative_arc: QUESTION (contrast hook): Open on a sharp before-after contrast — one side is the imagined input (a brief, a brand doc, a call, a strategy deck), the other side is the actual input (a website URL, typed in ten seconds). The contrast is stated plainly, no drama. ANSWER: The video explains directly that fenrik Studio reads the website, builds the content, and delivers a complete package — video, captions, hashtags, platform-ready for every channel — from that single input. No direction required from the client. WHY IT MATTERS: Most people never start because they are waiting until they have time to write the brief. That moment never arrives. The brief was always the invisible barrier. Here it does not exist. CTA: Submit the URL. The first package is free. There is nothing left to prepare.
emotional_tone: Matter-of-fact and quietly reassuring — no pressure, no urgency theater. The tone is a reporter stating a fact the audience did not know but immediately believes. Relief, not excitement.
audience_insight: The audience has mentally queued fenrik Studio under 'things I need to set up properly before I start' — alongside writing a brand brief, scheduling a discovery call, and deciding on a content strategy. That queue never clears. The video removes the queue entirely by showing that the setup they imagined was never required.

hook: What if the only thing you needed to start was just a URL?
scenario: A solo SaaS founder opens a new browser tab intending to finally submit their website to a content service. They get as far as the homepage before the familiar hesitation arrives — 'I should write up our tone of voice first. And figure out which platforms to prioritise. And probably get on a call to explain the product properly.' They close the tab. The account stays quiet for another two weeks. The setup they imagined was never required. The URL was always enough.
